author: Bernard Shambrook (family attribution)
auditScope: All 28 pages of the completed transcription, faithful text and editorial qualifications. This is a textual evidence audit, not external geographical identification or new handwriting transcription.
datePolicy: ISO dates are supplied only for legible day/month/year dates or dates securely anchored in the contiguous 1941 voyage account. Contextual year/day derivations are noted.
Tentative manuscript dates, ambiguous date associations, broad intervals and undated sketches have null dateISO.
Place spellings and question marks are retained; no coordinates are invented.
mapPolicy: Separate confirmed movements, tentative destinations, dated place notes and undated/tentatively dated sketches.
Passing a port does not establish docking or shore leave.
A line between points is at most a schematic sequence, never a reconstructed exact route.
Do not draw a continuous route across chronology gaps; incomplete or hypothetical links must be absent or explicitly labelled.
Address-book entries, grave/memorial dates, other people’s places, historical events and shipboard locations are not itinerary stops.

journeyEvents.dateDisplay: 6/5/41, about 4 pm; receiving depot that night

journeyEvents.summary: Left for the destination tentatively read [Rehovoth?].

journeyEvents.summary: Left the port tentatively read [Tewfic?]; HMT PP follows the date.

conflictsAndAmbiguities.description: IMG_0904 faintly reads Arrived [Suez?] [7/5/41?], with Gaza another possible place reading. IMG_0910/0911 clearly record arrival at Suez on May 3. The cover entry may not be a conflicting Suez date at all; May 7 is clearly recorded for Gaza and Kilo 89 elsewhere.

sources.excerpt:
May 3rd Saturday 4 pm arrived
Port Suez.

conflictsAndAmbiguities.displayRule: Use the clearer May 3 arrival as the main dated event and surface the uncertain alternative as a note; do not silently emend the transcription.

conflictsAndAmbiguities.description: Saturday, inserted 4th, Sunday and a partly illegible time-difference discussion coexist in IMG_0910. The editor cannot determine their intended correction from the text.

sources.excerpt:
3rd - owing to time difference. So on
Saturday [inserted: 4th] Sunday we are anchored in
Suez.

conflictsAndAmbiguities.displayRule: Show a stay interval with original wording available rather than assign each action to a forced date.

conflictsAndAmbiguities.description: Gaza arrival about 3 pm and Kilo 89 arrival are both dated 7 May, but there is no explicit timed connecting leg or statement that they are the same place.
conflictsAndAmbiguities.displayRule: Retain separate records; do not merge their coordinates or claim a precise same-day route.

conflictsAndAmbiguities.description: Julis and JULIUS occur in the two 17 May movement notes.
conflictsAndAmbiguities.displayRule: Use both source spellings in the evidence; any modern identification must be explicitly editorial and independently checked.

conflictsAndAmbiguities.description: The heading on IMG_0915 may be 23 September or 23 June 1941. The adjacent cemetery sketch has its own tentative [22/6/41?]. Photographic order does not resolve either date or establish one shared visit.
conflictsAndAmbiguities.displayRule: Keep the disputed heading date and tentative sketch date separate. Neither proves a dated visit; do not force either into the other’s chronology.

chronologyGaps: The notebook does not document every day or every stop; chronological and photographic order are different.
The Sydney–Fremantle–Ceylon sea legs give endpoints, not exact sailing tracks or positions.
Land sighted on 1 May is unnamed; no extra waypoint can be recovered from that sentence.
Kilo 89 requires historical location work; the notebook itself does not geolocate it or connect it precisely to Gaza.
The 25 May note records departure for [Rehovoth?], without an explicit arrival, restated origin or subsequent travel itinerary.
The June unit transfer has no geographic location; the 20 July note and 21 July hospital reference cannot securely fill the gap.
No route back to Port [Tewfic?] before 4 August is supplied; that departure has no destination in this notebook.
The 9/10 August note has no established location; it cannot supply the destination of the 4 August departure.
The Gaza heading has a disputed June/September date and cannot establish a route from the August departure.
Jerusalem War Cemetery and the Suez/Port Tewfic sketch have no dates and do not independently establish visits.
